title: From Niger Delta to the World: Our Wiki Loves Africa 2026 Story
content:
Nigeria’s Niger Delta is often introduced to the world through crude oil. The region is one of the country’s major oil-producing areas, but oil is only one part of its story.

Across the Niger Delta are communities with rich traditions, ceremonies, festivals, oral histories, music, dance, craftsmanship, and indigenous knowledge passed down through generations. Many of these practices are deeply connected to the identity of the people who preserve them. Still much of this cultural heritage is under-documented and, in an increasingly digital world, at risk of becoming less visible.

So, what happens when we look beyond the oil?

That was one of the questions that shaped our participation in Wiki Loves Africa 2026 campaign, whose theme, Rites & Rituals, invited Africans to document the cultural practices and traditions that define their communities.

For us, the campaign was an opportunity to tell a different story about the Niger Delta: one centred on its people, their cultures and the many rites and rituals that continue to shape community life.
snippet: Nigeria’s Niger Delta is often introduced to the world through crude oil. The region is one of the country’s major oil-producing areas, but oil is only one part of its story.
creator: Umasoye F. Igwe

title: Five sessions, five practical assignments, and a little more confidence with the technical side of Wikipedia: Wikimedia Ukraine’s course for tech skills
content:
In June and July 2026, Wikimedia Ukraine organized a Technical Skills Course for Wikipedia editors — a five-session online course designed to help contributors better understand and use some of Wikipedia’s technical tools.

Organizing learning activities for the Ukrainian Wikimedia community remains difficult because of the ongoing war. Air raid alerts, Russian attacks, and power outages can make it difficult or sometimes simply impossible to attend an offline event or even join an online session at a specific time.

That is why we designed the training as a course that participants could follow both live and asynchronously. People could join the webinars in real time, ask questions and discuss practical cases, while recordings were available afterwards for those who could not attend. If an air raid alert started during a webinar or the electricity went out, participants could return to the session later and continue learning at their own pace.

The course was led by three experienced members of the Ukrainian Wikimedia community.

title: Updates from the July 2026 Wikimedia Endowment Board Meeting
content:
The Wikimedia Endowment held its bi-annual Board meeting on 17 July 2026. The Endowment Board meets twice per year to provide governance, strategic direction, and stewardship of the Wikimedia Endowment’s assets.

The Board appointed Jordanna Polis Schutz as a new At-Large Director. 

Jordanna Schutz is an early-stage investor, entrepreneur and technologist with experience across emerging technologies, science-based innovation, and enterprise software.  She has a lifelong passion for how we develop, share, validate and negotiate knowledge.

She manages Pactolus Ventures and Birchaven Group, serves on the Board of Starfall Education Foundation, and enjoys volunteering with a youth ultimate frisbee program. Prior to her work in venture capital, she founded the online payment company Lucidity Inc. and held roles in both the private sector and U.S. federal government focused on technology, analysis, informational integrity, and emerging threats.

title: From Philology to Semantic Triples: Displaying Ancient Inscriptions with Digital Tools
content: This summer, I had the pleasure of serving as an intern for the IDEA Project, an initiative that documents information related to the ancient Syrian city of Dura-Europos. My job included transcribing and digitally representing a series of inscriptions from the Palace of the Dux Ripae, a military building created during the city’s Roman occupation in the third century. The inscriptions cover a wide range of functions: some were painted requests for the master of the house to be remembered, while others were mundane lists or messages scribbled on the walls by ancient passers-by. The inscriptions I worked on also vary in language, from Greek to Latin to Persian, reflecting the multilingual culture of the frontier city.

title: Dagbani Wikimedians User Group Introduces Community to Wikivoyage and Launches Wikivoyage Edit-a-thon
content:
The Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, in collaboration with African & Proud, has organized a two-part Wikivoyage training program aimed at introducing community members to Wikivoyage and encouraging the documentation of destinations, culture, history, and travel information from Ghana.

The project is a collaborative initiative between African & Proud and the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, bringing together their shared interest in promoting African knowledge, culture, and representation through open knowledge platforms. The collaboration seeks to equip community members with the skills to document places and travel experiences while increasing the visibility of destinations and local knowledge from Ghana on Wikivoyage.

The training was held on 8 August and 15 August 2026 through Zoom, with the first session focusing on an introduction to Wikivoyage and the second serving as a follow-up session and the official launch of a Wikivoyage edit-a-thon.

The first training session, held on 8 August 2026, introduced participants to Wikivoyage, a Wikimedia project that provides free travel information for travelers around the world by Dnshitobu.

title: More than 200 registrations, 22 speakers, and seven hours of shared experience: Wikimedia Ukraine’s Education Community Conference 2026
content:
On 15 August, Wikimedia Ukraine held its 2026 online conference for the Wikimedia education community, bringing together teachers, university lecturers, Wikimedia contributors, education professionals, and community organizers from across Ukraine.

More than 200 people registered for the conference, with around 60 participants online simultaneously during the day. The programme featured 22 speakers and more than seven hours of presentations, practical cases, and discussions.

Holding a long synchronous online event in Ukraine is still not something we can take for granted. Russia’s ongoing war continues to affect everyday life, including the stability of electricity and internet access. We did experience some connectivity problems during the conference, but speakers, organizers, and participants adapted — and we managed to complete the full programme.

title: Wikimedia LEADS: A Learning Ecosystem for the Wikimedia Movement
content:
The Wikimedia Movement has always been more than a collection of websites. It is a global learning environment where people discover how to write, cite, translate, discuss, organize, document, photograph, model data, preserve knowledge, and collaborate across cultures. Yet much of that learning still happens informally: through trial and error, local mentoring, scattered documentation, project pages, workshops, edit-a-thons, and community memory. Many in the movement have identified this phenomenon as a very big handicap for newcomer onboarding. And we need to face it.

Wikimedia LEADS proposes a way to make the learning explicit, findable, reusable, and recognized.

Presented as a proposal for the Wikimedia Hackathon 2026 in Milano, Wikimedia LEADS imagines a shared learning infrastructure for the Wikimedia Movement. Its purpose is not to replace existing Wikimedia learning practices, but to support them through practices, competences, course contents, learning activities, learning evidence tracking and credentials in a learning ecosystem for the people.

title: Wikimedia Foundation Bulletin 2026 Issue 15
content:
Here is a quick overview of highlights from the Wikimedia Foundation since our last issue on August 1. Previous editions of this bulletin are on Meta. Let foundationbulletin@wikimedia.org know if you have any feedback or suggestions for improvement!

  • Improving Account Creation process: As part of Account Creation Experiments an improved account creation form has been released. The form now provides live username validation, a clearer username policy popover, and a reveal password button. We also removed redundant elements and jarring warning messages, improved the form’s information hierarchy, and aligned the design with Codex design system guidelines.
  • Create charts from your own data: The new ChartWizard makes the Chart extension more beginner-friendly by allowing editors to create charts, such as bar and pie charts, without needing to use JSON. The ChartWizard is now available on Wikimedia Commons. Feedback on the new tool is welcome on the wish talk page.

    • See also: Growth · Product Safety and Integrity · Tech News · Language and Internationalization · The Wikipedia Library · list of movement events · Wikifunctions & Abstract Wikipedia

title: Wiki Town: Playas Doradas, Patagonia Argentina
content:
The community embraced the project and completed the installation of QR codes that link to Wikipedia articles. 

On July 25, residents of Playas Doradas (Río Negro, Argentina) walked through the town’s streets installing 38 new QR codes on street signs. Each code links a street name to the Wikipedia article about the species that gives it its name:trofón, buccino, jarillal, piquillines, among other plants and animals native to the Patagonian steppe. The event marked the conclusion of a phase of the project “Las calles de Playas Doradas”, (The Streets of Playas Doradas) spearheaded by WikiUNLP in collaboration with La Lechuza Community Library, Islote Lobos National Park (National Parks Administration), and Sierra Grande Department of Tourism. The project achieved something that doesn’t always happen: a community that embraced the initiative as its own

title: Sharing GLAM Experience: Annoda Gobinda Public Library, Pabna, Bangladesh
content:
Wikimedia Bangladesh is starting a new GLAM initiative at Annoda Gobinda Public Library in Pabna. The project is being led by MS Sakib.

I have been working with GLAM projects in Rajshahi for a long time. So, on 10 and 11 August 2026, I travelled more than 100 kilometres from Rajshahi to Pabna. The main purpose of the visit was to exchange my GLAM experiences with Sakib. Sheikh Mehedi Hassan also joined us during the visit. It was a great opportunity to learn from each other and discuss the practical challenges of GLAM work.

I brought a CZUR ET25 Pro scanner from Rajshahi. I had used this scanner in my own GLAM work before. From now on, Sakib and Mehedi will use it for book digitization at the library. I showed them the complete scanning process through a hands-on session. I also shared some practical techniques that I learned from my own experience. Both of them are talented Wikimedians. They learned the workflow very quickly.
snippet: Wikimedia Bangladesh is starting a new GLAM initiative at Annoda Gobinda Public Library in Pabna. The project is being led by MS Sakib.
creator: Mmrsafy

title: UNESCO and Wikimedia Movement Deepen Their Partnership at Wikimania 2026
content:
Wikimania 2026 in Paris marked an important step forward in the growing relationship between the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and the Wikimedia movement. Building on grassroots partnerships developed with UNESCO field offices, Wikimedia Foundation staff and Wikimédia France helped connect regional collaboration with colleagues at UNESCO headquarters, creating new opportunities for stronger institutional engagement.

Together with Alejandra Reyes (Wikimedia France), Michael David Miller (Université McGill et Wikimedia Canada) the Wikimania 2026 chair and co-chair of the Partners and Sponsors Committee, and Sakti Pramudya (Wikimedia Foundation), they formed a team that supported the coordination of these engagements, helping demonstrate how trust and partnerships developed at the local and regional levels can contribute to broader collaboration globally.
snippet: Wikimania 2026 in Paris marked an important step forward in the growing relationship between the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and the Wikimedia movement.

title: Call for Satellite Hosts: Wiki Indaba Hackathon 2026
content:
The Wiki Indaba Hackathon Committee is inviting Wikimedia communities, affiliates, user groups, universities, technology communities, and other organisations across Africa to host satellite locations for the Wiki Indaba Hackathon 13th to 15th November 2026.

A Satellite location is a space that will allow participants who cannot attend the main event in person to gather locally, collaborate on projects, and connect with the wider hackathon online.

We are looking for hosts who can provide:

  • A suitable space for participants for 2 to 3 days
  • Reliable internet connectivity for 2 to 3 days
  • Electricity or a power backup solution
  • A local person who can coordinate the satellite location
  • Basic coordination with the organising team

    • You do not need to have hosted a hackathon before. What matters most is having a suitable space, a reliable local contact, and an interest in supporting the Wikimedia technical community.

    Satellite hosts will:

  • Coordinate the local venue and participants
  • Ensure the space and connectivity are ready
  • Stay in contact with the Satellite Coordination Lead
  • Support participants during the hackathon
  • Help connect the local group with the main hackathon programme
snippet: The Wiki Indaba Hackathon Committee is inviting Wikimedia communities, affiliates, user groups, universities, technology communities, and other organisations across Africa to host satellite locations
